close_reason: Fixed: escape '%', '_', '\' in the literal prefix before building LIKE pattern; added ESCAPE '\\' to SQL. Test handle_list_underscore_in_reference_matches_literally confirms underscore is matched literally.
description:
Why this issue exists: imap/src/session/mailbox.rs handle_list() constructs a DB LIKE pattern from the client-supplied mailbox reference name. The reference name is bound via sqlx .bind() which prevents SQL injection, but the LIKE-special characters '%' and '_' within the literal prefix portion are not escaped (e.g. with '\' as ESCAPE char). A client sending LIST "a_b" "*" would match 'a1b', 'axb', etc. in addition to 'a_b'. In practice IMAP folder names rarely contain '_', but RFC 3501 §6.3.8 specifies that the reference argument is a literal string prefix, not a pattern.

What needs to be done: Escape '%' and '_' in the reference name before constructing the LIKE pattern, then append '%' to match any suffix. Use ESCAPE '\' in the SQL.
title: IMAP LIST: LIKE metacharacters in mailbox prefix not escaped before DB query
